headline_marked: Google Lyria 3.5: [[AI music generation]] now supports full-length songs via Gemini API
headline: Google Lyria 3.5: AI music generation now supports full-length songs via Gemini API
summary: Google's Lyria 3.5 model can now generate 44.1 kHz stereo music from text and image prompts, offering developers a more robust tool for creative workflows.
details: Google has upgraded its AI music generation capabilities with Lyria 3.5, now available in public preview via the Gemini API. This new version supports the creation of full-length songs at 44.1 kHz stereo quality, moving beyond the 30-second tracks previously possible.

Lyria 3.5 can generate music from both text and image prompts, offering enhanced musicality, improved vocals, and greater creative control. The model was first rolled out to Flow Music on July 29, 2026, with tempo and duration controls, before its subsequent release to the Gemini API.

This advancement provides developers and creative teams with a more direct path to integrate AI-generated music into their products and production workflows. The ability to generate longer tracks makes AI music more suitable for use in videos, podcasts, and other media where short clips are insufficient.

Google's SynthID technology is integrated to provide a provenance marker for AI-generated audio, making its origin more identifiable. While not a complete solution for all usage issues, it aids in tracking the source of generated content within Google's ecosystem.

The Gemini API integration is particularly significant for businesses aiming to streamline music creation as a repeatable process. Developers can potentially build workflows that connect prompt generation, track creation, human review, and asset delivery within existing applications.

Potential applications include generating draft background music for marketing videos, creating audio variations for campaigns, or producing initial music options for podcast intros. Image prompting may also help align audio generation with a campaign's visual direction.

Pricing for Lyria 3.5 is still being finalized, with specific costs for the Gemini API and Flow Music tiers not yet fully detailed. Businesses interested in implementation should consult current Google documentation for the most up-to-date pricing information.

For organizations exploring generative audio, Lyria 3.5's longer outputs and API accessibility make it a more compelling tool for reducing repetitive early-stage work while retaining editorial oversight.
